plan.title: fix(windows): path identity compares 8.3 short and long spellings in the shared git path helpers (#7199 A)

narratives.Description: On Windows one folder has several spellings: the long name, the 8.3 short name that os.tmpdir() returns on the CI runners, another letter case, or a junction path. Directive's path-identity checks in hook root admission, occupancy, the session ritual and swarm compare those spellings as strings, so one worktree looks like two and the session's own checkout is refused as foreign-repository. This story adds one win32 canonical-path helper in session/git.ts, routes every named identity compare and the worker-auth and spawn-reservation hash keys through it, and leaves POSIX code paths, recorded fields and dispatcher.ts message text unchanged.
narratives.Overview:
1. Helper. `packages/core/src/session/git.ts` exports `canonicalPathIdentity(path)` and `samePathIdentity(a, b)`. On win32, `canonicalPathIdentity` returns `realpathSync.native(path)`; when that fails with ENOENT or ENOTDIR it resolves the nearest existing ancestor natively and appends the missing rest unchanged; any other failure returns null. It keeps the native case and never folds case. `samePathIdentity` is true only when the two inputs are already equal under the site's existing compare, or both canonical forms are non-null and equal. On POSIX neither function is called by any site in this change, so every POSIX path keeps the function it uses today (`resolve`, JS `realpathSync`, or a fold).
2. Git helpers. On win32, `gitCommonDir`, `worktreePath` and `worktreePathOrNull` pass their result through `canonicalPathIdentity` and keep today's value when it returns null. The git argv is unchanged (no `--path-format`, so no git-version dependency and no test-mock churn). `mainWorktreeRoot` inherits the fix.
3. Identity compares. On win32 these compare through `samePathIdentity`: `admitEffectiveHookRoot` (both equality tests; on a match found only by canonical identity it returns the candidate, git's spelling, as the effective root) and the root de-duplication in `admitMutationTargetSet`; `occupancyWorktreeMatches` (`occupancyCanonicalPath` uses the helper on win32); the ritual-state worktree compare in `verify-session-ritual.ts` and `session-start.ts`; `restampOwnerLivenessOnHookEvent`; `sameRepoPath` and the alias-peer `physicalTargetKey` in `swarm/pre-dispatch.ts` (the key keeps its fold; the lexical ledger key `normalizeTargetId` stays lexical); `sameTree` in `worktree-pm-install.ts`, `main-worktree.ts`, `spawn-occupancy.ts` (including `existingDispatchReservation`) and `child-occupancy.ts`; the main-root compare in `swarm/dest-place.ts`; and the `resolveWorktreeMap` lookup against `git worktree list`, whose `compareKey` folds the canonical form exactly as it folds today. The local `sameTree` / `sameRepoPath` copies are replaced by one shared export that keeps each site's current behavior plus the win32 identity test.
4. Hash keys. On win32, worker-auth `canonicalWorktreePath` (used by write, reuse match, cleanup, and the reader through `resolveWorkerAuthDestPath`) and spawn `reservationDigestKey` (reserve, read, release) build their key from `canonicalPathIdentity`; the reservation key keeps its case fold. For git's long spelling of an existing worktree the key is the same as before. Nothing looks up a pre-fix key. Residual, named: a worker-auth record written before the fix under a non-canonical spelling stays an unread orphan file (the reader already never found it), and a spawn lock written before the fix under such a spelling is not seen by a later reserve, so a reservation live across the upgrade can be doubled once, the same split two spellings cause today.
5. Storage and messages. Recorded fields keep what they record today; no record is rewritten and no migration runs. No refusal or message text in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` changes; only path spellings inside existing messages may change. Write-target containment, the write fence and the protected-destination realpath checks do not use the helper.
6. Docs. `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md` says that on win32 the payload root and candidate roots compare by physical identity (a junction or 8.3 spelling of the same checkout is that checkout), that write targets are still not canonicalized (#4023 unchanged), and that no case fold applies to roots.
7. Tests (win32, skipped when no 8.3 name exists for the fixture folder, found with `cmd /c for %I in ("<path>") do @echo %~sI` and checked to resolve to that folder): the helper (8.3, lowercase, missing leaf, a failure other than ENOENT or ENOTDIR gives null and adds no equality); `gitCommonDir`; and one 8.3 case per family: admission, ritual compare, owner-liveness, `isMainWorktreePath`, pre-dispatch alias peer, spawn reservation key, worker-auth key, `resolveWorktreeMap`; POSIX tests are unchanged.
8. One PR: `git.ts` and the files in items 3 and 4, their tests, the doc in item 6 and one `changelog.d/` fragment. Install, upgrade, doctor, setup, launcher and uninstall code is not touched; the one edit in `swarm/worktree-pm-install.ts` is the identity guard of linked-worktree preparation (`sameTree`), not package-install logic. After merge the nightly Windows lane decides the five probable files; each still red gets its own issue with Refs #7199.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/core/src/session/git.ts` exports `canonicalPathIdentity` and `samePathIdentity`; on win32 an 8.3 spelling and a lowercase spelling of one existing folder give the same canonical form as its long spelling, a missing leaf (ENOENT or ENOTDIR) keeps its spelling under the native ancestor, any other failure gives null, and null adds no equality beyond the site's existing compare.
- [ ] On win32, `gitCommonDir`, `worktreePath` and `worktreePathOrNull` return the helper's form when it resolves and today's value when it returns null, so `gitCommonDir` from the 8.3 spelling of a main worktree equals the value from its long spelling and from a linked worktree of the same repository.
- [ ] Given a payload root in 8.3 spelling and a write target in the same main worktree or in a linked worktree of the same repository, `admitEffectiveHookRoot` admits; a target in a different repository is still refused `foreign-repository`; no case fold is applied to roots.
- [ ] On win32, occupancy, the ritual-state worktree compare, owner-liveness re-stamp, `isMainWorktreePath`, linked-worktree prep, dest-place, story binding (`sameRepoPath`), the pre-dispatch alias-peer check, spawn and child occupancy, and `resolveWorktreeMap` treat an 8.3 spelling and the long spelling of one worktree as the same worktree, each proven by a test that is skipped where 8.3 names are unavailable.
- [ ] Worker-auth keys (write, reuse match, cleanup and read) and spawn reservation keys (reserve, read and release) are the same for the 8.3 and long spellings of one worktree and unchanged for the long spelling; no code path looks up a pre-fix key.
- [ ] The 34 confirmed files listed in the issue pass on the nightly Windows lane; each of the 5 probable files passes or gets its own issue with Refs to #7199.
- [ ] POSIX behavior is unchanged: no POSIX branch changes, and the Linux nightly and the merge gate stay green.
- [ ] No refusal or message text in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` changes, and `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md` states that roots compare by physical identity on win32 while targets are still not canonicalized (#4023).
narratives.Constraint:
- The issue's store-canonical plan (rewrite recorded paths): inputs that never pass through git (hook payload roots, spawn destinations, cohort maps, worker-auth inputs) need the compare anyway, and rewriting records adds a mixed-spelling period for no gain.
- `--path-format=absolute` for `gitCommonDir` (Stop 1 R1): it adds a git-version dependency whose refusal is not detectable by exit status, and it breaks exact-argv test mocks; the helper on today's output gives the same spelling.
- Long-name-only expansion (`GetLongPathNameW`): Node does not expose it without a native call or a spawn, and it leaves letter case and junctions to each site.
- Pre-fix-key lookups for old worker-auth records and spawn locks (lean 7105017639 item 4; audit 7105125739 findings 1 and 2): a complete version needs new reader logic and a search across spellings, and old non-canonical records are no worse than today without it.
- Case folding inside the identity helper: it can make two case-distinct repositories equal at admission's first test.
- Setting TEMP/TMP to the long path in CI: it hides the bug.
narratives.UserStory: As a Windows user or CI runner whose TEMP or cwd uses an 8.3 short name, I want Directive's path-identity checks to treat every spelling of one worktree as the same worktree, so that hooks, occupancy, the session ritual and swarm stop refusing my own checkout.

2. On win32 pass gitCommonDir, worktreePath and worktreePathOrNull results through the helper, keeping today's value on null and the git argv unchanged.
3. Replace the local sameTree / sameRepoPath copies with one shared export and route the named compares through samePathIdentity: admitEffectiveHookRoot and admitMutationTargetSet, occupancyWorktreeMatches, the ritual compare in verify-session-ritual.ts and session-start.ts, restampOwnerLivenessOnHookEvent, sameRepoPath and physicalTargetKey, worktree-pm-install.ts sameTree only, main-worktree.ts, spawn-occupancy.ts, child-occupancy.ts, dest-place.ts and resolveWorktreeMap. Do not change any refusal or message text in dispatcher.ts.
4. Build the worker-auth canonicalWorktreePath key and the spawn reservationDigestKey from canonicalPathIdentity on win32; add no pre-fix key lookups.
5. Update content/docs/hook-root-admission.md for win32 root identity and the unchanged #4023 target rule.
6. Add win32 tests that skip when no 8.3 name exists: the helper and gitCommonDir in session/path-identity.test.ts, and one 8.3 case per family in its existing test file; run the verify_commands on Windows and Linux; add one changelog.d fragment; regenerate RULE-MAP, PROJECT-DEFINITION, evaluator-surface disposition and the spec-drift row only if the build changes them.

## In plain English
On Windows one folder can have several spellings: the long name (`C:\Users\runneradmin\...`), the 8.3 short name (`C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...`, which `os.tmpdir()` returns on the CI runners), a different letter case, or a path through a junction. Directive's path-identity checks compare these spellings as plain strings, so they treat one worktree as two. The hook then refuses writes as "a different Git repository", the ritual check says the state "belongs to a different worktree", swarm says a worktree is "not a worktree of this repository" or "not a registered git worktree", and `session:start` exits 1. On the nightly Windows lane this is 39 test files and 258 tests; for a real user it is a false denial whenever the cwd or TEMP is not in git's spelling.

The parent measured this on a Windows box at the dispatch SHA (see Evidence). Git itself already prints the canonical long path for `--show-toplevel`, so `worktreePath` and `worktreePathOrNull` are not the source. The source is `gitCommonDir`: for a main worktree git prints a relative `.git`, which the helper joins onto the caller's spelling. The other source is call sites that compare a caller's spelling with git's spelling. A lowercase spelling of the same folder fails the same way as an 8.3 spelling.

The parent recommends: ask git for the absolute common dir, add one identity helper on win32 that both sides of every identity compare pass through, compare canonical forms instead of rewriting what is recorded, and change no message text. The critics are asked to weigh this against the issue's `realpathSync.native` everywhere plan, and to check that admission still refuses a foreign repository.

## Pains
- P1 — On Windows, when the cwd, TEMP or a recorded path spells a worktree differently from git (8.3 short name, other letter case, junction), path-identity checks treat one worktree as two: hook root admission returns `foreign-repository`, the ritual check reports a different worktree, swarm reports not-a-worktree / not-registered / `foreign-worktree`, and `runSessionStart` exits 1 (#7200 body; nightly Windows lane, 39 files / 258 tests).

## Out of scope (named, not pains)
- Refusal and message text in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` (polfer's area). Only the comparison changes; path spelling inside existing messages may change.
- Install, upgrade, doctor, setup, launcher, uninstall and `--root` discovery (polfer's area; the umbrella's P3 group). Those may reuse the helper later; this fix does not edit them.
- Test fixtures that assert a raw tmpdir 8.3 spelling (#7202) and `payloadIsOwnGitRoot` (#7201). They follow this fix's canonical form in wave 2.
- Setting TEMP/TMP to the long path in CI or vitest setup. That hides the bug.

## Evidence (parent measurements on this host, git 2.55.0.windows.3, Node 24.18.0)
- `C:\Repos\deft\DIRECT~1` is the 8.3 name of `C:\Repos\deft\directive`. From that cwd: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` prints `C:/Repos/deft/directive`; `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` prints `.git`. From `c:\repos\deft\directive` (lowercase) and from a junction to the checkout, the toplevel is again `C:/Repos/deft/directive` and the common dir is again a relative `.git`. From a linked worktree the common dir is the absolute long path `C:/Repos/deft/directive/.git`.
- `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` prints `C:/Repos/deft/directive/.git` from the 8.3 cwd, its subfolder, and the lowercase cwd. The flag is already used in `packages/core/src/presentation-coverage/isolated-scope.ts` (`--path-format=absolute --git-path objects`).
- `fs.realpathSync.native("C:\\Repos\\deft\\DIRECT~1")` returns `C:\Repos\deft\directive`, and it fixes letter case; `fs.realpathSync` (the JS form) returns the 8.3 spelling unchanged; `realpathSync.native` throws ENOENT on a missing path. Both forms resolve a junction to its target.
- The pinned `admitEffectiveHookRoot` (source read from the primary checkout, where `dispatcher.ts` and `git.ts` are identical to the pin), with the real git runner: payload `C:\Repos\deft\directive` admits a target in the linked worktree `C:\Repos\deft\wt\arc-7200` and a target in the main tree. Payload `C:\Repos\deft\DIRECT~1` refuses both with `foreign-repository`, including the target in its own main tree. ## Problem

On Windows, path-identity checks compare an 8.3 short path (`C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...`, from `os.tmpdir()` or the caller's cwd) with git's long path (`C:/Users/runneradmin/...`) as strings. The two spellings name the same folder, but the checks treat them as different trees.

How the mismatch happens:
- `worktreePath` / `worktreePathOrNull` (`packages/core/src/session/git.ts`) return git's `--show-toplevel`, which is the long path.
- `gitCommonDir` returns `.git` relative for a main worktree, so it is resolved against the caller's short spelling. For a linked worktree, git returns an absolute long path. `admitEffectiveHookRoot` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`) then compares the two common dirs and calls a linked worktree of the same repo `foreign-repository`.
- Occupancy records `worktreePath: resolve(projectRoot)` (`occupancy.ts`), but the ritual check compares the recorded path with `worktreePath()` output (`verify-session-ritual.ts:364`, `session-start.ts:824`).
- `sameRepoPath` (`packages/core/src/swarm/pre-dispatch.ts:327`) only lowercases, and `resolveWorktreeMap` keys (`packages/core/src/swarm/worktrees.ts`) do not match `git worktree list` output.

Observed symptoms on the nightly Windows lane:
- `write target is in a different Git repository than the hook payload root` for a linked worktree of the same repo
- `session ritual state belongs to a different worktree`
- `story-binding: no record written (target): ... is not a worktree of this repository`
- `which is not a registered git worktree`, and `git worktree add` fails because the folder `already exists`
- `prepareLinkedWorktree` returns `foreign-worktree`; `runSessionStart` exits 1

A Windows user whose `TEMP` or cwd uses an 8.3 name hits the same denials. This is a product bug.

## Scope (39 files / 258 tests)

hooks: `dispatcher-effective-root` 30, `dispatcher-spawn-dest` 23, `dispatcher-merge-gate-warn` 18, `dispatcher-active-scope` 12, `dispatcher-story-binding` 7, `story-binding-in-pr-completion` 5, `dispatcher-outside-root` 4, `dispatcher-owner-liveness` 2.
session: `occupancy` 21, `verify-session-ritual` 15, `spawn-occupancy` 11, `compact-ritual` 7, `branches` 4, `session-start-consumer-root` 3, `occupancy-stale-ritual-recovery` 3, `verify-session-ritual-branches` 3, `extra-coverage` 2, `package-manager-network` 2, `main-worktree` 2, `child-occupancy` 1, `coverage-boost` 1, `inspect-session-ritual` 1, `session-start` 1, `verify-session-ritual-default-runner` 1.
swarm: `complete-cohort-sweep` 16, `worker-auth-assignment` 15, `pre-dispatch-story-binding` 11, `worktrees` 8, `worktree-pm-install` 5, `dest-place` 4, `swarm-deep-coverage` 1.
other: `core/scm/worker-auth-cli.integration` 4, `runtime/gates-cli/session-ritual-cli` 5, `runtime/hook-dispatch-worktree` 2.
probable, re-check after the fix: `core/orphan-active/candidate-scope` 4, `runtime/hook-host-identity-lifetime` 1, `runtime/dispatch-pack-root` 1, `runtime/plan-sequence-bound-push` 1, `core/tutorial/cli` 1.

## Likely fix site

Add one canonical-path helper in `packages/core/src/session/git.ts`. On win32 it uses `realpathSync.native`, which expands 8.3 names; when the path does not exist yet, it falls back to the nearest existing ancestor. `worktreePath`, `worktreePathOrNull` and `gitCommonDir` return the canonical form. Path-identity comparisons and recorded paths use the helper: `normalizeHookProjectRoot`, occupancy `worktreePath` records, ritual-state compare, `sameRepoPath`, and `gitWorktreeList` keys. Linux is green today, so keep POSIX behavior unchanged.

Constraints:
- Do not change refusal or message text in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`; that text is in another owner's area. Path spelling inside existing messages may change.
- Do not set `TEMP`/`TMP` to the long path in CI or vitest setup as the fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/core/src/session/git.ts` exports one canonical-path helper, and `worktreePath`, `worktreePathOrNull` and `gitCommonDir` return its form on win32.
- [ ] Hook root admission (`admitEffectiveHookRoot`), occupancy records, the ritual-state worktree compare, `sameRepoPath` and `resolveWorktreeMap` compare canonical paths, not raw strings.
- [ ] A unit test proves that an 8.3 short spelling and the long spelling of one worktree compare equal on win32 (skipped where 8.3 names are unavailable).
- [ ] The 34 confirmed files listed above pass on the nightly Windows lane.
- [ ] Each of the 5 probable files passes, or gets its own issue with Refs to #7199.
- [ ] POSIX behavior is unchanged: the Linux nightly and the merge gate stay green.
- [ ] No refusal or message text in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` changes.

Refs #7199, #7172

acceptance.derived_reason: one clause per harvested lean item (16), in list order (#6333)
sentences: Helper. `packages/core/src/session/git.ts` exports `canonicalPathIdentity(path)` and `samePathIdentity(a, b)`. On win32, `canonicalPathIdentity` returns `realpathSync.native(path)`; when that fails with ENOENT or ENOTDIR it resolves the nearest existing ancestor natively and appends the missing rest unchanged; any other failure returns null. It keeps the native case and never folds case. `samePathIdentity` is true only when the two inputs are already equal under the site's existing compare, or both canonical forms are non-null and equal. On POSIX neither function is called by any site in this change, so every POSIX path keeps the function it uses today (`resolve`, JS `realpathSync`, or a fold).

Git helpers. On win32, `gitCommonDir`, `worktreePath` and `worktreePathOrNull` pass their result through `canonicalPathIdentity` and keep today's value when it returns null. The git argv is unchanged (no `--path-format`, so no git-version dependency and no test-mock churn). `mainWorktreeRoot` inherits the fix.

Identity compares. On win32 these compare through `samePathIdentity`: `admitEffectiveHookRoot` (both equality tests; on a match found only by canonical identity it returns the candidate, git's spelling, as the effective root) and the root de-duplication in `admitMutationTargetSet`; `occupancyWorktreeMatches` (`occupancyCanonicalPath` uses the helper on win32); the ritual-state worktree compare in `verify-session-ritual.ts` and `session-start.ts`; `restampOwnerLivenessOnHookEvent`; `sameRepoPath` and the alias-peer `physicalTargetKey` in `swarm/pre-dispatch.ts` (the key keeps its fold; the lexical ledger key `normalizeTargetId` stays lexical); `sameTree` in `worktree-pm-install.ts`, `main-worktree.ts`, `spawn-occupancy.ts` (including `existingDispatchReservation`) and `child-occupancy.ts`; the main-root compare in `swarm/dest-place.ts`; and the `resolveWorktreeMap` lookup against `git worktree list`, whose `compareKey` folds the canonical form exactly as it folds today. The local `sameTree` / `sameRepoPath` copies are replaced by one shared export that keeps each site's current behavior plus the win32 identity test.

Hash keys. On win32, worker-auth `canonicalWorktreePath` (used by write, reuse match, cleanup, and the reader through `resolveWorkerAuthDestPath`) and spawn `reservationDigestKey` (reserve, read, release) build their key from `canonicalPathIdentity`; the reservation key keeps its case fold. For git's long spelling of an existing worktree the key is the same as before. Nothing looks up a pre-fix key. Residual, named: a worker-auth record written before the fix under a non-canonical spelling stays an unread orphan file (the reader already never found it), and a spawn lock written before the fix under such a spelling is not seen by a later reserve, so a reservation live across the upgrade can be doubled once, the same split two spellings cause today.

Storage and messages. Recorded fields keep what they record today; no record is rewritten and no migration runs. No refusal or message text in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` changes; only path spellings inside existing messages may change. Write-target containment, the write fence and the protected-destination realpath checks do not use the helper.

Docs. `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md` says that on win32 the payload root and candidate roots compare by physical identity (a junction or 8.3 spelling of the same checkout is that checkout), that write targets are still not canonicalized (#4023 unchanged), and that no case fold applies to roots.

Tests (win32, skipped when no 8.3 name exists for the fixture folder, found with `cmd /c for %I in ("<path>") do @echo %~sI` and checked to resolve to that folder): the helper (8.3, lowercase, missing leaf, a failure other than ENOENT or ENOTDIR gives null and adds no equality); `gitCommonDir`; and one 8.3 case per family: admission, ritual compare, owner-liveness, `isMainWorktreePath`, pre-dispatch alias peer, spawn reservation key, worker-auth key, `resolveWorktreeMap`; POSIX tests are unchanged.

One PR: `git.ts` and the files in items 3 and 4, their tests, the doc in item 6 and one `changelog.d/` fragment. Install, upgrade, doctor, setup, launcher and uninstall code is not touched; the one edit in `swarm/worktree-pm-install.ts` is the identity guard of linked-worktree preparation (`sameTree`), not package-install logic. After merge the nightly Windows lane decides the five probable files; each still red gets its own issue with Refs #7199.

`packages/core/src/session/git.ts` exports `canonicalPathIdentity` and `samePathIdentity`; on win32 an 8.3 spelling and a lowercase spelling of one existing folder give the same canonical form as its long spelling, a missing leaf (ENOENT or ENOTDIR) keeps its spelling under the native ancestor, any other failure gives null, and null adds no equality beyond the site's existing compare.

On win32, `gitCommonDir`, `worktreePath` and `worktreePathOrNull` return the helper's form when it resolves and today's value when it returns null, so `gitCommonDir` from the 8.3 spelling of a main worktree equals the value from its long spelling and from a linked worktree of the same repository.

Given a payload root in 8.3 spelling and a write target in the same main worktree or in a linked worktree of the same repository, `admitEffectiveHookRoot` admits; a target in a different repository is still refused `foreign-repository`; no case fold is applied to roots.

On win32, occupancy, the ritual-state worktree compare, owner-liveness re-stamp, `isMainWorktreePath`, linked-worktree prep, dest-place, story binding (`sameRepoPath`), the pre-dispatch alias-peer check, spawn and child occupancy, and `resolveWorktreeMap` treat an 8.3 spelling and the long spelling of one worktree as the same worktree, each proven by a test that is skipped where 8.3 names are unavailable.

Worker-auth keys (write, reuse match, cleanup and read) and spawn reservation keys (reserve, read and release) are the same for the 8.3 and long spellings of one worktree and unchanged for the long spelling; no code path looks up a pre-fix key.
The 34 confirmed files listed in the issue pass on the nightly Windows lane; each of the 5 probable files passes or gets its own issue with Refs to #7199.
POSIX behavior is unchanged: no POSIX branch changes, and the Linux nightly and the merge gate stay green.

No refusal or message text in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` changes, and `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md` states that roots compare by physical identity on win32 while targets are still not canonicalized (#4023).
